verdict.pair_reasons:
X vs Y — Y wins on five verified, material differences. (1) Y is the only output to hit K19: scripts/handoff-fire.sh:9493 `fable) MODEL="$(_ssot_scalar frontier_access model)"` — the alias resolves from the same SSOT key the gate reads. X never cites handoff-fire.sh's model logic at all. (2) Y gets K2's full precision — fails OPEN on a MISSING SSOT, CLOSED on a present-but-unreadable one — which I reproduced (chmod 200 on the config → rc=2, `active=unset, end=unset`). X instead asserts in §5 that the window-closed branch "is unreachable in production unless `active` is manually flipped to `false`", which that same probe refutes; that is the direct answer to brief item 5. (3) Y alone turns the same fact into a refutation of migrations/0029:39-40's own blast-radius claim ("fails OPEN everywhere … a missing/unreadable SSOT") — verified false for the unreadable half. (4) Y catches two bypasses X misses entirely, both explicitly demanded by brief item 6: the quoted `--model "fable"` spelling (M5 — I confirmed the :75 extractor returns nothing) and TMPDIR/counter-file tampering (M6). (5) Y catches the stale citation INSIDE the enforcer (M8, gate:27 → handoff-fire.sh:9303-9311, which is `hf_inflight_key`, verified at :9304-9318) plus a bad citation neither other output found (L1-census.md:61 attributing an opus fallback to :9493, the `fable)` branch). X's compensating strength is real — config/hook-chains.d/pretooluse-bash:7-8/:18-27 is a second, LIVE-derived artifact confirming the gate's absence from the Bash matcher, which neither Y nor Z has — but it does not offset five key items plus a measured-wrong reachability claim. X also asserts a false absence ("source … none appear anywhere" — it is at :26) and miscounts the CC_LADDER grep as two hits when it is three lines.

X vs Z — Z wins, narrowly but on specifics. Z hits four key items X misses: M5 (quoted-model bypass), M8 (the gate's own stale self-citation at :27), M10 (three verified true-of-code/false-of-wiring sentences — skills/frontier-routing/SKILL.md:40-42, gate:2, and the sharp handoff-fire.sh:9506 find), and partially M6. Z also states what the closed-window session message would actually EMIT today (the full id `claude-opus-5-5`, contradicting the alias discipline test 13 enforces on the sibling message) — a live-behaviour conclusion X's §5 stops short of. And Z avoids X's one materially wrong claim, correctly noting that a missing frontier_access block makes the branch refuse ("that direction fails closed"). Against that, Z carries three off-by-one citations, one of them load-bearing (model-config.yaml:700 for `fallback: claude-opus-5-5`, which is :699), shares X's false `source` absence claim, and its §8 sweep is thinner — it misses p15-escalation.md:44, A5-harness.md:357, A6-mechanics.md:245 and :500, and L1-census.md:62, all of which X checks and characterises correctly. Net: 31 key items vs 27, plus no reachability error, beats the wider doc sweep and the hook-chains find.

Y vs Z — Y wins. Y hits K19 and Z does not; Y alone states K2 in the both-directions form the key flags as the precision point and alone converts it into a verified refutation of migrations/0029's own claim; Y alone catches L1-census.md:61's misattributed citation; Y alone explains why running install.sh does NOT close the registration gap (install.sh:1203-1204, :1216-1218, :29 — all verified verbatim) and alone spots that the migration's header verify/conflict oracles read one config dir while the body writes five, producing a strictly better answer to brief item 7's "one command". On citation hygiene Y is cleanest of the three: I found no bad citation and no wrong claim, and its absence claims are narrowly scoped to `start` and `permanent` (both genuinely absent), where Z widened the same claim to `source` and was wrong. Z's genuine edge is M10 — its three-instance sweep, especially handoff-fire.sh:9506, is the best treatment of that item in any of the three — but Y states the same defect via gate:2 and CLAUDE.global.md:334, so the gap is coverage depth on one item against Z's four off-by-one/false citations and its K19 miss.
